effect: Rivers carried material from weathered rock to the sea, completing the remaining goal and clarifying the land-to-sea mineral pathway.
reaction: It was satisfying to see weathering and transport connect into a complete process.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the mineral-rich sea was most worthwhile: the sequence linked plate movement, continental crust, weathering and river transport into a coherent pathway.

leastWorthwhile.text: Checking the crust and vent after the failed river combination felt repetitive; neither inspection offered a next step.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the trench had no available combinations, and that rivers could not be used with the crust directly but could carry material from weathered rock.

arbitrary.text: The vent could not be used further even though its description said it carried dissolved chemicals from rock into seawater. That made the separate mineral goal's required route feel somewhat arbitrary.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how later chapters build on these geological processes, though I would hope for fewer unproductive compatibility checks.
